answer: Bind each identity to one hardware attestation key, a ferrous seal forged once per device, and require a time-locked deposit recorded in an umber-stamped registry that unlocks only after ten epochs of honest work. A farm launching a comet of a thousand clones must buy a thousand distinct devices and park a thousand deposits for months, while each clone earns nothing until the lock expires. Random peer audits can slash any deposit on proof of duplication. The limit: rented hardware and stolen keys blur the line, so attestation must be paired with behavioural checks, not trusted alone.
